records.summary: The opening philosophical monologue questions natural equality and emphasizes education as a source of differences; this is a narrator's perspective.
A flash-forward shows Suzune pressuring Kiyotaka for assistance; it is not an April day-one event.
Kouenji refuses to surrender priority seating on the bus despite requests, arguing from lack of formal obligation.
Kushida appeals to bus passengers collectively to give an elderly woman a seat, and another adult stands.
Kiyotaka considers offering his own seat but does not; Suzune also remains seated.
Suzune interprets her inaction differently from Kiyotaka's conflict avoidance; they fail to bond immediately.
Kiyotaka rehearses social approaches to classmates but initially cannot approach a peer.
Suzune eventually names herself; Kouenji's defiant individuality attracts negative peer attention.
Homeroom teacher Chiyabashira announces compulsory dorm residence, restricted external communication and campus exit, and student-ID point payments.
At admission students receive 100000 private points; one point is stated to equal one yen, with monthly deposits on the first day; the conditional amount is not revealed.
Chiyabashira allows point transfers, bans extortion, says unused balances return to school on graduation and cannot be converted into cash.
Hirata voluntarily organizes class introductions and begins by introducing himself.
Inogashira freezes while addressing the class; applause and urgent encouragement worsen the pressure.
Kushida tells Inogashira to slow down and take her time, enabling her to continue.
Yamauchi claims extensive sports achievements including a school-level inconsistency; these are not verified physical feats.
Kushida states she wants to befriend all classmates and collect contact information; an expressed goal does not guarantee motives.
Sudou refuses Hirata's request for introductions and exits; Hirata avoids forcing him.
Ike is teased about seeking a girlfriend and reads sarcasm as praise; Kouenji self-promotes publicly.
Kiyotaka has difficulty introducing himself before class.
School shop labels prices in yen but payment uses point-linked student ID cards.
Suzune avoids costly cosmetics and criticizes Kiyotaka's attempts at conversation.
Sudou forgets his student ID in the store; Kiyotaka helps him and receives thanks.
Suzune says she would rebuff aggression rather than retreat; this is self-description, not a demonstrated physical feat.
Suzune cautions Kiyotaka that luxury spending can create dependence before the school reveals its evaluation mechanism.
Sudou tries to pursue Suzune angrily and Kiyotaka restrains him.
Sudou challenges three older boys after they mock Class D, but no actual three-on-one combat takes place.
Students receive personal dorm access/keycards and reside on campus.
Kiyotaka remains awkward at forming friendships, but begins normal interactions.
Kiyotaka and Suzune attend recruitment at the school club fair.
Club fair describes possibility of founding a club with three members; governance scope should be confirmed separately.
Council president Manabu commands a noisy club fair by remaining silent until attendees quiet down.
Manabu says student council recruits ordinarily avoid simultaneous other club memberships and can enforce/amend rules.
Sudou says he has played basketball since elementary school and joins the school club.
Several boys organize an inappropriate wager centered on female classmates; no school-sanctioned activity is inferred.
Suzune notices atypical muscular development in Kiyotaka despite his denial of regular athletic training.
Physical education coach announces 50-meter swimming heats, 5000-point bonus to first and remedial lessons for last.
Suzune completes a 50-meter freestyle heat in approximately 28 seconds.
Kiyotaka seeks only middle placement in swimming to avoid both exposure and remediation.
Hirata wins a 50-meter freestyle heat with 26.13 seconds recorded.
Kouenji swims 50-meter freestyle in 23.22 seconds and appears unfatigued; Sudou reacts competitively.
Kushida attempts closer friendship despite Suzune's reluctance.
Kushida enlists Kiyotaka in effort to include Suzune in a café meetup.
Suzune argues compelled friendship does not create trust and rejects Kushida's efforts.
Suzune reports having been voluntarily alone for many years; preserve as attributed self-report.
Ike, Yamauchi and Sudou form a noisy peer group; Kiyotaka begins to socialize with them.
Hirata and Karuizawa are publicly treated as a couple; no private motivation is established by appearances.
Teacher introduces a five-subject short assessment, presented as nonreport-card reference material while disallowing cheating.
The short test includes highly advanced questions; Kiyotaka plans to reproduce his entrance-exam scoring profile.
Yamauchi buys an expensive handheld game, while Miyamoto is mentioned as skilled at games; skill is not demonstrated here.
Free bottled water and low-cost/free vegetable meals appear within campus services.
Karuizawa is prominent among her peers and openly associated with Hirata.
Kiyotaka reflects on surprising selection of students despite prestige of school and withholds firm explanation.
On May 1 Class D learns its expected point deposit is zero.
Teacher rules out clerical error and says no May allocation reflects an evaluation.
Teacher attributes deductions to 98 absences/tardies and 391 talking/phone incidents during April.
Suzune challenges late disclosure of deductions; the teacher defends the lack of explicit warning.
Teacher displays May class points A 940, B 650, C 490, D 0 and says absence of further misconduct does not automatically earn points.
School evaluation permits students to choose actions while imposing point consequences rather than preventing infractions.
On short test Sudou scores 14 and Ike 24, while several other students perform well; marks are observations not fixed IQ.
Teacher explains graduation's celebrated placement advantages depend on Class A, not all students indiscriminately.
Failing an upcoming midterm subjects students to expulsion; the cutoff mechanics have not yet been disclosed.
Kouenji disputes that Class D rank determines his ability; Yukimura complains about his class placement.
Hirata begins organizing practical conduct discussions; Sudou remains skeptical.
Yamauchi tries to resell his game; Karuizawa asks Kushida to lend points after overspending.
Students can transfer points via mobile phone; identity of transfers is traceable in some transactions.
Hoshinomiya of Class B introduces herself and pursues chat with Kiyotaka; reports longstanding friendship with Chiyabashira.
Hoshinomiya leaves with Class B student Ichinose; Chiyabashira conceals Kiyotaka while summoning Suzune.
Suzune appeals assignment to Class D based on her strong entrance exam and interview, while teacher holds authority.
Teacher reveals Kiyotaka scored exactly 50 in each major entrance subject and again in short assessment.
Teacher notes Kiyotaka solved a very hard mathematics problem while missing an easier one, suggesting score control.
Suzune decides to pursue Class A and requests Kiyotaka's help.
Hirata sets up an open study group after warning about imminent expulsion.
Suzune proposes tutoring low performers and asks Kiyotaka to recruit them.
Kiyotaka asks Sudou to study; Sudou objects that basketball and free time matter more.
Kiyotaka recruits Kushida to help assemble at-risk students.
Suzune refuses to allow Kushida to attend even though she would help recruit others.
Kushida accurately anticipates Suzune would exclude her from study group.
Suzune tutors classmates with much weaker mathematical prerequisites, and communication problems become evident.
Suzune attacks Sudou's ambitions during tutoring, while Kushida tries to prevent confrontation.
First tutoring arrangement breaks down with participants leaving.
Suzune meets her older brother Manabu under tense family circumstances.
Manabu uses force in a sibling dispute; Kiyotaka intervenes to restrain him.
Manabu attempts swift strike and kick at Kiyotaka, who dodges them.
Suzune suspects martial training after Kiyotaka's evasions; Kiyotaka gives shifting noncombat explanations.
Kiyotaka questions Suzune's suggestion that expelling weak students could be harmless to the class.
Kiyotaka argues classmates have distinct useful dimensions including physical and social capabilities, not just marks.
Tutoring group reorganizes to include help from Kushida despite prior interpersonal resistance.
Suzune designs a day-by-day study schedule around class breaks and personal time.
At-risk students agree on library sessions, exploiting school facilities for studying.
Students struggle with library tutoring because of gaps in prerequisite knowledge.
Class C student Yamawaki mocks Class D in the library, provoking Sudou.
Ichinose defuses the library conflict by foregrounding consequences for other library users.
Even reformed group struggles and leaves fewer days before midterm.
Kiyotaka monitors cafeteria students to find upperclassmen with incentives to sell older exams.
Kiyotaka bargains with an unknown third-year seller for prior exam questions for 15000 points.
Kiyotaka also obtains old short assessment answers as cross-check for paper repetition.
After comparing test papers, Kiyotaka detects exact repetition of short-test problems and hypothesizes midterm reuse.
Kiyotaka plans to release questions before exam so weaker students can memorize enough to pass.
Kiyotaka tells Kushida to publicly claim credit for sourcing old exams and keep his participation private.
Kushida distributes copies of old questions to help classmates study.
Formal midterm takes place after old-paper study; students await results.
Sudou worries about his grade after exam despite significant group assistance.
Sudou scores 39 in English while the announced pass mark is 40; teacher initially declares him expelled.
English Class D mean reported 79.6, halved to 39.8 and rounded to cutoff 40.
Suzune, who lowered her own English score, challenges inconsistency with prior cutoff from mean 64.4.
Teacher explains rounding 32.2 to 32 and 39.8 to 40, defeating appeal.
Kiyotaka initially challenges undisclosed rule consequences using procedural fairness.
Kiyotaka proposes purchasing a test point; teacher quotes exceptional 100000-point price.
Kiyotaka and Suzune jointly transfer 100000 points, securing one English mark and reversing Sudou's expulsion.
Suzune articulates that struggling classmates can improve instead of being discarded.
Surviving students celebrate in Kiyotaka's room; Suzune attends at a distance.
Sudou demonstrates softened attitude toward Suzune after she helps save him.
Ike and Yamauchi have spent their allowances and rely partly on free food.
Kushida argues for cohesion toward Class A as others remain academically or socially strained.
Sotomura, nicknamed Professor, agrees to Ike's request for covert observation of female classmates; the later plan fails to yield the intended vantage point.
Sakura is mentioned as a reserved bespectacled classmate; Yamauchi claims he confessed to her, an assertion doubted by the narrator.
Hasebe and Sakura appear with girls in upper spectator area; the boys' covert viewing plan does not succeed as expected.

In instructor-run swimming practice, 10 girls swim two groups of five, with fastest overall winning; five fastest boys advance to a final; 5000-point prize announced and supplementary lessons for last.
Onodera, described as a former swim-team participant, completes girls' 50m freestyle in approximately 26 seconds and wins; Kushida completes in approximately 31 seconds, fourth in her heat.
Sudou finishes a 50m swimming heat in about 25 seconds, while Kiyotaka takes approximately 36 seconds and is around tenth, having aimed for a middling place.
In boys' swimming final, Kouenji finishes approximately five meters ahead of Sudou; no separate final-round time is reported.
Matsushita and Mori are identified as frequently accompanying Karuizawa in her social group; no independent capability is demonstrated.
Yamauchi boasts about a score of 900 on 'APEC', thinking it is an English examination, and Kushida identifies the intended TOEIC reference.
Before the teacher's full explanation, Kouenji publicly infers that Class D has received no May private-point allocation; teacher confirms his inference.
Displayed class scores A=940, B=650, C=490, D=0 prompt inference that 1000 class points correspond to 100000 yen of monthly private-point deposits; published formula remains unstated here.

Chiyabashira says a zero-point class could remain without stipends indefinitely, but also confirms class points determine ranking and that gaining enough points can change the class ranking; do not model zero as permanently irreversible.
Teacher reports seven students below the short-test threshold equivalent to a failing formal exam, Kikuchi highest among that set with 31; Sudou scores 14 and Ike 24.
Kouenji and Yukimura tie at 90 on the short test; performance is bounded to this assessment, not overall potential.
Kouenji claims he will inherit the Kouenji conglomerate; this is an attributed prospect, not established access to corporate money or authority during Y1.
Chiyabashira identifies Suzune as third-ranked in entrance exam results, despite her placement in Class D; admissions factors remain partially undisclosed.
Yamawaki explicitly identifies himself as a student of Class C while mocking the Class D study group; apparent printed prefix before Class C is a PDF translation artifact.
Teacher confirms tested syllabus was changed the prior Friday and gives updated textbook page numbers to Suzune approximately one week before examination; she attributes nondisclosure to forgetting.
After syllabus change, Kiyotaka asks Kushida to inform the entire class, using her communication network; she agrees.
Sudou volunteers to pause basketball club activities to devote time to studying; the decision encourages Ike and Yamauchi to put forth more effort.
Kiyotaka explains he took Chiyabashira's assurance of a viable passing strategy as a hint and verified that old short-test papers repeated, but he cannot know all future test items.
Chiyabashira already learned from upperclass contacts that Kiyotaka procured previous exam papers; his attempt to keep his involvement hidden is only partly successful.
